item.title: UWF Argos Cap FCS Inaugural Season With Win Over West Georgia
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida football program closed out its first season in the Football Championship Subdivision on a high note Saturday, defeating West Georgia in what organizers are calling the inaugural "Borderline Brawl." The matchup featured contrasting halves, according to reporting from North Escambia, with UWF's offense executing a…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida football program closed out its first season in the Football Championship Subdivision on a high note Saturday, defeating West Georgia in what organizers are calling the inaugural "Borderline Brawl."

The matchup featured contrasting halves, according to reporting from North Escambia, with UWF's offense executing a season-defining touchdown drive late in the game. The Argos' defense also delivered a crucial stop to seal the victory and punctuate their historic first year at the FCS level.

The win marks a successful conclusion to UWF's transition from Division II to the FCS, the highest level of NCAA football below the Football Bowl Subdivision. The Argos are still working to establish themselves in their new conference and build a rivalry with West Georgia, which the two programs have designated with the "Borderline Brawl" branding.

item.title: Warm Sunday Ahead Of Scattered Showers Monday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Northwest Florida is in for a mild Sunday before weather conditions shift early next week. Expect mostly sunny skies today with highs near 76 degrees and light northwest winds becoming calm through the afternoon, according to the National Weather Service North Escambia forecast. Monday brings a change, with scattered showers and storms possible…
item.content:encoded:
Northwest Florida is in for a mild Sunday before weather conditions shift early next week. Expect mostly sunny skies today with highs near 76 degrees and light northwest winds becoming calm through the afternoon, according to the National Weather Service North Escambia forecast.

Monday brings a change, with scattered showers and storms possible throughout the day. The extended outlook shows growing potential for more widespread rainfall by midweek before conditions improve heading into the Thanksgiving holiday.

Patchy fog is possible Sunday night after 2 a.m., so early morning drivers should use caution. Cooler and drier conditions are expected to settle in after the midweek rain clears out, making for pleasant weather through the holiday period.

item.content:encoded: Drivers in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should expect construction-related slowdowns on several state roads this week as maintenance crews continue work in the area. On Escambia County's State Road 292 (Gulf Beach Highway), intermittent lane closures are expected between Bauer Road and Manchester Street as crews perform construction and maintenance activities. Drivers are urged to allow extra time for commutes through affected areas and to watch for work zones. Additional state road construction is underway in Santa Rosa County as well, though details on those projects were not immediately available. The Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) typically staggers work during daylight hours to minimize traffic impact, though lane closures may occur during peak and off-peak times.

item.title: Farm to City event delivers Thanksgiving meals to 1,000 families Tuesday

item.content:encoded:
More than 1,000 families across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties will get a complete Thanksgiving meal next week through the annual Farm to City Food Distribution, a drive-thru event scheduled for Tuesday, November 24, starting at 9 a.m.

Participants can pick up their meals at locations in both Pensacola and Milton, making the program accessible to residents throughout the region. The event is part of the organization's ongoing effort to address food insecurity and ensure families have access to holiday meals during the Thanksgiving season.

Families interested in participating should plan to arrive during the drive-thru window. For specific location details and any additional information about the distribution, residents are encouraged to contact Farm to City or check local community resources.

item.title: Escambia County Jobless Rate Stays at 4.7% in October
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County's unemployment rate held steady at 4.7% in October, according to data released Friday by the Florida Department of Commerce. The rate remained unchanged from September, suggesting relative stability in the local job market even as the broader economy shows signs of cooling. Nonagricultural employment in the county totaled 203,300…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County's unemployment rate held steady at 4.7% in October, according to data released Friday by the Florida Department of Commerce. The rate remained unchanged from September, suggesting relative stability in the local job market even as the broader economy shows signs of cooling.

Nonagricultural employment in the county totaled 203,300 positions last month, down 400 jobs compared to October 2025—a year-over-year decline of 0.2 percent. While the drop is modest, it reflects a slight contraction in the job base over the past twelve months.

The steady unemployment rate comes as economic data continues to be watched closely across Northwest Florida. Escambia County's 4.7% rate remains in line with regional trends, though local workforce conditions will likely continue to draw attention from business leaders and policymakers as the year closes.

item.content:encoded:
Northview High School's Navy Junior ROTC program captured first place overall at the Battle at Blakeley Orienteering Meet, earning the unit a spot in the upcoming Area Championship. The strong performance reflected the cadets' skill in orienteering, a navigation-based competitive sport that tests map-reading and tactical movement across outdoor terrain.

Beyond the top overall trophy, Northview's NJROTC squads also secured second-place finishes in both the Orange and Green course categories, demonstrating depth across multiple competitive teams. The win marks a significant achievement for the North Escambia program and positions the cadets to represent the school at the next level of regional competition.

item.title: Pensacola Zoning Board Rejects Veterinary Clinic Buffer Reduction
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Local residents opposed the proposal, citing concerns about potential flooding and drainage problems if the buffer were scaled back. The narrow vote…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Zoning Board voted 4-3 to deny a request that would have reduced the landscape buffer requirement for a new veterinary clinic, according to a report from Citizen Portal News Florida.

Local residents opposed the proposal, citing concerns about potential flooding and drainage problems if the buffer were scaled back. The narrow vote margin underscores the split sentiment around the project among board members.

The decision keeps existing landscape buffer standards in place for the proposed clinic. No additional details about the specific location or the clinic operator were immediately available.

item.content:encoded:
The iconic UFO House on Pensacola Beach has earned a spot in the video game world: Rockstar Games included the distinctive landmark in Grand Theft Auto VI, which launches later this year.

The UFO House—officially known as the Pensacola Beach House and recognizable by its flying saucer-shaped design—joins other Florida locations featured in GTA6's map. The game, one of the most anticipated releases in the industry, will include not just Miami but other recognizable spots across the state.

The inclusion adds to the UFO House's pop culture footprint. The structure, built in 1974, has become a well-known Pensacola Beach landmark and tourist attraction, with its unconventional architecture drawing visitors and media attention over the decades.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Landfill Operating Cash-Only Due to Internet Issues
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Santa Rosa County Central Landfill is operating on a cash-only basis Saturday due to internet connectivity problems that have knocked out its electronic payment processing system, according to a county alert issued this morning. Staff at the scale house are processing every transaction manually, which means visitors should anticipate longer…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Central Landfill is operating on a cash-only basis Saturday due to internet connectivity problems that have knocked out its electronic payment processing system, according to a county alert issued this morning.

Staff at the scale house are processing every transaction manually, which means visitors should anticipate longer wait times. County officials are asking residents to bring cash and have patience as the technical issues persist.

The Central Landfill, located in Santa Rosa County, maintains regular hours Monday through Saturday from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. For more information, residents can visit www.santarosa.fl.gov/351/Central-Landfill. The county has not announced when normal payment processing will resume.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola City Council unanimously approved consideration of reallocating $448,000 in American Rescue Plan funds to help Opening Doors Northwest Florida acquire a facility, according to Citizen Portal News Florida.

The 6-0 vote signals council support for the proposal, though the reallocation still requires formal approval. Opening Doors Northwest Florida is a local nonprofit focused on addressing housing and homelessness in the region.

American Rescue Plan funding has been designated for pandemic recovery and community support initiatives. The timeline for final approval has not been detailed, but the source indicates urgency around the decision.

item.title: ReadyKids! Gets $1.39M Boost, Named Nonprofit of the Year
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: ReadyKids!, a Pensacola-based early literacy nonprofit, is marking a major expansion phase with nearly $1.4 million in new funding and community recognition. The organization announced Friday that it received a Bright Beginnings grant from Escambia Children's Trust worth up to $463,000 annually over three years—totaling $1.39 million in possible…
item.content:encoded:
ReadyKids!, a Pensacola-based early literacy nonprofit, is marking a major expansion phase with nearly $1.4 million in new funding and community recognition. The organization announced Friday that it received a Bright Beginnings grant from Escambia Children's Trust worth up to $463,000 annually over three years—totaling $1.39 million in possible funding. The money will support ReadingPals, the organization's signature one-on-one mentoring program, while strengthening Pre-K offerings and expanding into additional Escambia County schools.

ReadyKids! also earned Nonprofit of the Year honors from EntreCon and Studer Community Institute at this year's awards celebration, recognizing the organization's investment in young learners and community partnerships. The group additionally received a $3,000 mini grant from MenPact of Pensacola to expand volunteer mentor connections through ReadingPals.

Executive Director Kristy Craig said the funding marks "a defining moment" that lets the organization "think bigger" and expand its reach. ReadyKids! has grown beyond its traditional Pre-K focus into kindergarten classrooms, supported by continued United Way funding through its Healthy Schools Escambia initiative. Founded in 2007, the nonprofit serves children and families across Escambia County. Those interested in volunteering as a ReadingPal mentor can visit ReadyKidsFL.org.

item.title: UWF Creates New Division of University Operations and External Affairs
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida has announced the establishment of a new Division of University Operations and External Affairs, consolidating key operational and administrative functions under one leadership structure. The reorganization, announced Friday, brings together essential campus services including facilities management, police, emergency…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida has announced the establishment of a new Division of University Operations and External Affairs, consolidating key operational and administrative functions under one leadership structure.

The reorganization, announced Friday, brings together essential campus services including facilities management, police, emergency management, military services, communications, and external relations. UWF President Manny Diaz Jr. said the restructuring reflects efforts to streamline operations and better serve the university community. "This new division reflects that work, establishing a structure that brings together key functions, encourages greater collaboration and positions UWF to operate more effectively," Diaz said in a statement.

Alex Smith, who previously advised the university president on strategic initiatives, will lead the division as senior vice president. In the new role, Smith will oversee University operations, governmental and external relations, institutional strategy, and presidential initiatives. The division will house eight major operational areas, from the Board of Trustees Office to Parking and Transportation, as well as University Marketing and Communications and the Office of Military Services.

Smith said the consolidation will improve coordination across departments. "Connecting our efforts more closely will help us anticipate needs, share information and address challenges together," he said. More information about the division is available at uwf.edu/oea.

item.title: Florida Executes 20th Inmate This Year, Breaking Modern Record
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida carried out its 20th execution of 2026 on Thursday, surpassing the state's modern-era record for most capital punishments in a single year. Thomas Mitchell Overton, 71, was pronounced dead by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Raiford at 6:19 p.m., according to North Escambia reporting. Overton had been sentenced to death for the…
item.content:encoded:
Florida carried out its 20th execution of 2026 on Thursday, surpassing the state's modern-era record for most capital punishments in a single year. Thomas Mitchell Overton, 71, was pronounced dead by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Raiford at 6:19 p.m., according to North Escambia reporting.

Overton had been sentenced to death for the murder of a Tavernier couple more than three decades ago. The execution marks a significant milestone in Florida's criminal justice system and reflects the state's accelerated pace of capital punishment this year.

The case remains under investigation by the Sheriff's Office. Anyone with additional information about the incident is encouraged to contact ECSO.

item.title: Tate High School Names Band Hall After Legendary Director Bill Slayton

Slayton by naming the band building at Tate High School the "Bill Slayton Band Hall." Slayton's decades of leadership and influence on the Tate High music program earned him recognition from the school district. The naming recognizes his…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County School Board has officially approved a resolution honoring former band director William E. Slayton by naming the band building at Tate High School the "Bill Slayton Band Hall."

Slayton's decades of leadership and influence on the Tate High music program earned him recognition from the school district. The naming recognizes his contributions to music education and his impact on generations of students who passed through the program.

The resolution was approved at a recent school board meeting, making the honor official. The Bill Slayton Band Hall will serve as a lasting tribute to Slayton's legacy at Tate High School.
